newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel gains on dollar, basket.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel gains on dollar, basket.

text.p: The Israeli shekel rose moderately against the dollar and the basket of key foreign currencies on Wednesday following two days of heavy losses, dealers said.
"Activity continues to be strong, but trading was very mixed with slightly more conversions of shekels into dollars," said a dealer at Israel Discount Bank.

"The shekel traded in a tight range. Whenever the dollar reached 3.2920 shekels investors started selling dollars," he said, adding: "The volatility in forex trading abroad had no impact on the local market."
The U.S. currency rose sharply on Monday and Tuesday from a rate of 3.253 on Friday. There is no foreign currency trading in Israel on Sunday.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.2900 shekels against 3.2920 on Tuesday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, closed at 3.6661 shekels against 3.6702 on Tuesday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.9043 shekels per 100 yen against 2.8867 on Tuesday and against the mark at 2.1082 shekels against 2.1062 on Tuesday.
In late afternoon the dollar was trading at 3.2880 shekels.
